subject: pe
title: Muscles & Bones: Major Bones
welcome_lead: From femur to skull — the bones you'll hear named in sports medicine.
meta_desc: KS3 PE: femur, tibia, humerus, cranium, vertebrae.
final_note: Naming bones helps you talk safely about injuries.

concepts.def: Thigh bone — longest in the body.

walkthroughs.body_html: The femur is the longest bone. Below the knee, the tibia (shin) bears most weight; the fibula is alongside.
The humerus runs from shoulder to elbow. Below it, the radius and ulna run to the wrist.
Stacks of vertebrae form the spine, protecting the spinal cord. The cranium protects the brain.

mcqs.q: Which energy system fuels a marathon?
options: Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
They are different names for the same component.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.

mcqs.q: Which type of muscle is under voluntary control?
options: Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
